selections.comment: This looks a match between the lightly raced pair Kilmore Rock and CRUDEN. The former was given a fine ride from the front last time in first time cheekpieces and he remains well treated on his novice form despite a 6lb rise. The latter is open to plenty of improvement on his handicap debut following a wind op. He has already shown a useful level of form on the flat and over hurdles in Ireland making this opening mark of 111 look generous. Though he is flat bred he has shaped like a stayer and can outclass these rivals if that proves to be the case.

selections.comment: Preference is for AMERICAN AFFAIR, who progressed well last season and is still on a competitive mark despite having bagged a big pot in the Portland at Doncaster on his penultimate start. Though he has been off for seven months, the fact that he was a C&D winner on his return last April augurs well for this 5yo, whose profile suggests could be a better horse this year. Cover Up has been running well in better company than today's at Meydan most recently and is next best ahead of the selection's old rivals Jer Batt and Jm Jungle.

selections.comment: This could be another punch-up between ONLY SPOOFING, Knicks and Zarzyni. The first-name won narrowly last time here six days ago and in theory is worst handicapped having gone up 4lb while the other pair remain on unchanged marks. However, Knicks got the best trip that day in a messy race, the selection only getting daylight late and getting up near the line while Zarzyni was closing fast on both having had no run from the back. Intriguing, but Only Spoofing is taken to hold Zarzyni again.

selections.comment: John Betjeman and Opticality are closely matched on their Taunton meeting last month and both should be on the premises. The former has dropped to an attractive mark and was unlucky not to be a fair bit closer next time as his rider dropped his whip late. A first time visor could spark a further revival. The latter is entitled to come on for that last run and has plenty of mileage in his mark given he was a flat winner last spring. The pair could be vulnerable to Dexter who returns to hurdling after a poor spell over fences. He has dropped to a very attractive mark based on his French form and could spring a surprise now returned to favourable soft ground.

selections.comment: ROYAL JEWEL gave an 18l beating to the future Greatwood Gold Cup winner at the turn of the year and he did very well to finish as close as he did last time after a series of errors. He will relish this step back up in trip and with Cobden taking over will be tough to beat. Heltenham failed to complete last time when outstayed over 3m but he did run well for a long way that day and has dropped a long way in weights. His yard is firing in the winners in pursuit of the title and he should go close to adding another. Scarface has proven generally consistent and was only narrowly denied in a stronger race last time. He can make his presence felt once more if the rain stays away.

selections.comment: WYVERN could be the solution to a tight affair. He's been in good nick this year and should be forgiven a slghtly below par effort last time when dropped badck to 7f. The step back up to a mile will help and he is 1lb below his last winning mark at a course and distance he's gone close over a couple of times. The son of Bated Breath has a solid chance. Top-weight Billy McGarry is an obvious danger. This hat-trick seeking, course and distance winner must be feared but he's never scored off a mark this high so Dappeld Light may lay down the biggest challenge to the selection. He won here over a furlong extra last time out but the drop back in trip should be no issue and he's entitled to be bang there again

selections.comment: Experience is likely to tell here with three previous winners the ones to concentrate on despite their 7lb penalty in this. RED SAND sets the standard and will be hard to beat if wound up for this return. The extra furlong is no issue, if anything it'll help, so if he copes with the Tapeta surface he should win. Warrior Mode has a fitness edge having won over course and distance on debut a month ago and is feared most. Jolly Roger, the third of the previously winning trip, looks a decent prospect having won on second start on Polytrack at Kempton in December when last seen. Like the selection he wil go close if fit and able to cope with a new surface. Wave Rider loooks best of the others with experience and could serve it up to this trio with a handy 7lb edge and is taken to reach the frame ahead of Jolly Roger.

selections.comment: A back to form GINCIDENT should take some beating having proved he's got the pace for 7f when landing the spoils at Leicester off a break earlier this month. Twice here over 1m James Owen's gelding could be on the march to rediscover former levels and has solid claims from a good draw. Ultramarine looks next best. He's disappointed the last twice over 6f but eased slightly in grade and returned to 7f he looks set to bounce back at at track that suits well and go close. The admirably consistent Novak poses a big threat but How's the Guvnor may offer a bit better value. He tried to make all last time here over 1m but had to use up too much energy from the widest berth before folding and can be excused that effort off a layoff. Much better is expected and he's on a dangerous mark if rediscovering some verve soon

selections.comment: The one that takes the eye is AUNTIE JOE. David O'Meara's filly has to be forgiven a poor effort last time (probably raced on unfavoured part of track) but looked to have found her level prior to that blip. Given further respite from the handicapper she's poised on a very threatening mark on the balance of her form since December and could reward backers. Royal Accord just about sets the standard and proved his well-being with a smooth win a week ago over 6f at Lingfield. However, the drop back to 5f on this sharp track could be his undoing and the risk is too big for given he won't go missed in the market. Wee Mary may prove a bigger threat. She went well on handicap bow in early April showing good pace to lead and kept on gamely before being over-hauled late in the closing stages. From stall two on a sharper track she's a potent threat in a weak affair
